interpretation: Single-trial comparison favours the analytic warm start (55 vs 54/60 first-trial convergence); production reaches 56/60 only via its second retry trial, which the analytic arm does not get. The three shared failures (11206, 13265, 33356) are solver-wide hard regions the emulator also cannot close. So for the stated goal (remove the emulator, keep the (m,T) solver stable, exactness not required) the H2 analytic warm start is not merely viable but strictly competitive with the emulator on first-trial convergence, at zero runtime cost for a neural net. The paper-level exactness claim (deep 7000-8000 K p95 <= 0.02 dex) remains unmet.
question: Does an emulator-free analytic (m,T) warm start (H2 formula) reach solver-stability parity with the production emulator warm start on the same 60 stars?

single_trial_comparison.merit: A warm start that converges on its FIRST solver trial needs no retry; the single-trial comparison is the cleanest measure of warm-start quality because production is allowed up to 2 trials while the analytic arm is allocated exactly 1.
single_trial_comparison.note: On a first-trial basis the emulator-free analytic warm start is at least as good as the emulator warm start (55 vs 54). Production only reaches parity on the full result because it is allowed a second retry trial; the analytic arm is not. Full 60-star totals for reference: analytic 55/60, production 56/60 (after retries).
